title: Christian Living - Episode 2: Work as Worship

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Hello again, and welcome to the SleepFit podcast series. <short pause> You're listening to Christian Living, episode two: Work as Worship. <chuckle> I'm David Lee, and I'm glad you're here. <short pause> Before you drift off tonight, let's think about tomorrow for a moment... <short pause> what if the work waiting for you in the morning is already a way of worshipping God?

Paul wrote to ordinary believers in Colossae... people who woke up to ordinary days. <short pause> Some were servants in households. Some worked in fields, or workshops, or kitchens. <short pause> Their labor wasn't always noticed. <short pause> It wasn't always thanked. <short pause> And Paul said something that turned all of it inside out.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men; Knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for ye serve the Lord Christ. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Whatsoever you do. <short pause> Not just the work that feels important, or noble. <short pause> Not only the tasks you'd choose if you could. <short pause> Whatsoever.

The meeting you're dreading. <short pause> The email you need to write. <short pause> The floor you need to sweep. <short pause> The errand that takes longer than it should. <short pause> The conversation that will test your patience.
Do it heartily, Paul says. <short pause> Do it with your whole heart.

That word means more than effort. <short pause> It means you're all in... not split in two. <short pause> Not going through the motions while your mind is somewhere else. <short pause> Not counting the minutes, or nursing resentment, or wishing you were anywhere but there.
Heartily means you show up to the work in front of you as though it matters. <short pause> Because it does. <short pause> Not because someone is watching... but because of who you're working for.
As to the Lord, and not unto men. <long pause>

This is the turn. <short pause> This is what makes a stack of invoices, or a load of laundry, into something more. <short pause> You're not ultimately working for a boss, or a client, or even for yourself. <short pause> You are working for the Lord.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: That changes the nature of the work. <short pause> It doesn't change the work itself. <short pause> The spreadsheet is still a spreadsheet. The dishes are still dishes. <short pause> But when you do them as to the Lord... they become an offering.

Think about what that means for tomorrow. <short pause> The task that feels small, or repetitive, or beneath your gifts... you can do it as an act of love toward God. <short pause> The project that frustrates you, where no one seems to care about excellence... you can still care, because he sees. <short pause> And the work you do in secret, the part no one will ever applaud... he knows.

Paul goes on. <short pause> Knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance. <short pause> There is a reward... but it doesn't come from the people you serve. <short pause> It comes from the one you're truly serving.

This isn't about earning heaven. <short pause> That has already been settled, by grace. <short pause> This is about how faithfulness in small things is seen, and remembered, by God. <short pause> He doesn't miss the tenth time you choose patience. <short pause> The twentieth time you do good work, even when you're tired. <short pause> The hundredth time you serve without credit.
For ye serve the Lord Christ. <long pause>

That's the center of it. <short pause> Not a principle... but a person. <short pause> You're serving Christ in the middle of your Monday. <short pause> In the weariness of your Wednesday. <short pause> In the long stretch of your Thursday afternoon. <short pause> He is there in it... and he receives it.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: <exhales> So tonight, as you think about tomorrow... you don't have to divide your life into sacred and secular. <short pause> You don't have to wait for a special assignment to live for God. <short pause> The work in front of you, the ordinary work, can be done as worship.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Not perfectly. <short pause> Not without frustration, or failure. <short pause> But heartily. <short pause> As to the Lord.

And when you do, something quiet and true happens. <short pause> You stop performing for people... and start offering your work to God. <short pause> You stop measuring your worth by outcomes... and start resting in the fact that you are seen. <short pause> You stop waiting for your real life to begin... and start recognizing that this, right here, is where faithfulness lives.

Let's pray. <short pause> Lord, tomorrow I will work... and I ask that you would help me work as unto you. <short pause> Teach me to see the ordinary as an offering... and to do it with my whole heart.
Rest well tonight. <short pause> Goodnight.
